_comment: Jev questions for design slop evaluation. Uses Score primitives for Signature (S1-S7) and Cohesion (H1-H4) axes, plus Noul for Quality Checklist verification.

signature_s1_artifact.instructions: Evaluate the signature artifact. Is there ONE high-effort focal object (crafted SVG scene, populated product artifact, illustration, render) that could only belong to this brand? Consider: Could this visual be pasted onto another site without modification?
levels: 0 — Absent: No custom focal object; hero is text on a fill or stock/prop visual
50 — Attempted: A custom visual exists but is generic enough to paste onto another site
100 — Strong: ONE high-effort focal object that could only belong to this brand

signature_s2_atmosphere.instructions: Evaluate the atmosphere. Is the background a composed environment (scene, texture, grain, light) carried down the whole scroll? Or is it flat color fills?
levels: 0 — Absent: Flat color fill behind everything
50 — Attempted: Some texture/tone in the hero only (dies at the fold)
100 — Strong: Background is a composed environment carried down the whole scroll

signature_s3_layered_depth.instructions: Evaluate layered depth. Is there foreground copy / midground focal object / background scene, with at least one element overlapping or bleeding across a layer edge?
levels: 0 — Absent: One flat plane
50 — Attempted: Two reads, nothing crossing a boundary
100 — Strong: Three layers with at least one element overlapping/bleeding across

signature_s4_character_face.instructions: Evaluate the display typeface. Is there a licensed/self-hosted display face with real personality, set large, chosen for this brief? Or does identity rest on a neutral grotesque or Google-shelf default?
levels: 0 — Absent: Identity rests on neutral grotesque or Google-shelf default (Inter, Space Grotesk, Poppins)
50 — Attempted: A distinctive face chosen by reputation, not brief (Fraunces, DM Serif)
100 — Strong: Licensed/self-hosted display face with real personality, chosen for THIS brief

signature_s5_bespoke_silhouette.instructions: Evaluate bespoke silhouettes. Is there one unmistakable custom-cut geometry signing the page? A receipt-torn edge, an invented marker, a specific arrow drawn for the system?
levels: 0 — Absent: Every shape is a default rectangle/pill
50 — Attempted: One mild customization (a radius decision, a simple notch)
100 — Strong: One unmistakable custom-cut geometry signing the page

signature_s6_treated_nav.instructions: Evaluate the navigation treatment. Is the nav a decision: floated pill, real presence, brand marks threaded in — does it belong to the system? Or is it a default flush row bolted on top?
levels: 0 — Absent: Default flush row of links bolted on top
50 — Attempted: Centered or contained but generic
100 — Strong: The nav is a decision: floated pill, real presence, brand marks threaded in

signature_s7_real_specificity.instructions: Evaluate real specificity. Are there real recognizable logos honestly claimable, real names/data inside product shots, copy written for this product? Or placeholder logos, fake names, lorem-adjacent copy?
levels: 0 — Absent: Placeholder logos, fake names, lorem-adjacent copy
50 — Attempted: Mixed — some real data among placeholders
100 — Strong: Real recognizable logos, real names/data, copy written for this product

cohesion_h1_palette.instructions: Evaluate palette discipline. Is there a monochrome or tightly-related color set where adjacent sections share or hand off tone? Or 'blue AND green AND warm accent', each fine alone, ugly together?
levels: 0 — Absent: Multiple unrelated color families fighting (blue AND green AND warm accent)
50 — Attempted: Palette exists but sections don't hand off tone consistently
100 — Strong: Monochrome or tightly-related set; adjacent sections share or hand off tone

cohesion_h2_type_voice.instructions: Evaluate type voice consistency. Is there a single family across weights/optical sizes, or one display + one quiet neutral? Or two display faces arguing?
levels: 0 — Absent: Two or more display faces arguing, no typographic system
50 — Attempted: Type system exists but inconsistent application
100 — Strong: Single family across weights/sizes OR one display + one quiet neutral consistently applied

cohesion_h3_one_system.instructions: Evaluate component system unity. Do nav, buttons, arrows, radii, borders, backgrounds speak one language? Sharp everywhere, one arrow reused, one gradient threaded through? Or mismatched fine components that read cheap?
levels: 0 — Absent: Mismatched components — different radii, arrow styles, border treatments
50 — Attempted: Some consistency but breaks in places
100 — Strong: One language — consistent radii, arrows, borders, treatments throughout

cohesion_h4_from_brief.instructions: Evaluate if sections were designed from what this product actually is — not known skeletons restacked, not a reference site's content reproduced. Reference = direction, never a stencil.
levels: 0 — Absent: Known skeletons restacked and recolored, or reference site reproduced
50 — Attempted: Some sections respond to content, others are template fills
100 — Strong: Every section designed from what this product actually is

quality_evidence_inventory.instructions: Is the evidence inventory complete? Documented what was captured (code, screenshots, live URL) and what is Unverifiable?

quality_brief_documented.instructions: Is the brief documented? If provided, summarized in report header; if not provided, noted as 'no brief'?

quality_context_identified.instructions: Is the design context identified? What type of design is this (landing page, SaaS dashboard, editorial, e-commerce)?

quality_references_read.instructions: Were all reference files read before sweeping? (tells.md, premium-markers.md, contexts.md)

quality_cite_or_cut.instructions: Is cite-or-cut enforced? Every recorded tell has ID + severity + concrete citation (hex value, font name, file:line, or screenshot region)?

labels.yes: Every tell has concrete evidence citation

quality_premium_pair_checked.instructions: Before recording any tell, was premium pair checked? Verified it's not the crafted premium version of the pattern?

labels.yes: Premium pairs checked before recording tells

quality_portability_test.instructions: For borderline cases, was portability test applied? 'Could this element be moved to another site without alteration?' If yes → tell. If no → not a tell.

labels.yes: Portability test applied to borderline cases

quality_defense_test.instructions: For borderline cases, was defense test applied? 'Could the designer defend this choice with concrete reasoning?' If no → tell. Slop cannot be defended.

labels.yes: Defense test applied to borderline cases

quality_section_attribution.instructions: Is every tell assigned to a specific section (Hero, Features, Pricing, Footer, etc.) for the Section Ledger?

quality_severity_discipline.instructions: Is severity discipline maintained? Critical reserved for absolute-rule violations only; no severity inflation?

quality_exclusions_documented.instructions: Is every excluded tell documented with a justification tag (// BRIEF:, // DESIGN DECISION:, // CONTEXT:, // PREMIUM PAIR:)?

quality_exclusions_genuine.instructions: Are exclusions genuine? 'We liked it' or 'it looked good' are NOT valid. Only explicit brief direction or documented design decisions with concrete reasoning qualify.

labels.yes: Exclusions are genuine with concrete reasoning
labels.no: Some exclusions are vague or unjustified

quality_exclusions_count.instructions: Is the exclusion count reasonable? If >5 tells excluded, each should be double-checked. >10 suggests something is wrong.

labels.yes: Exclusion count reasonable (≤5 or each justified)
labels.no: Exclusion count excessive (>5 without scrutiny or >10)

quality_unverifiable_marked.instructions: Are all unverifiable checks marked? Not silently passed or skipped?

quality_absolute_rules_reported.instructions: Are all 6 absolute rules reported with pass/fail/unverifiable and evidence?

labels.yes: All 6 absolute rules reported with evidence
labels.no: Some absolute rules missing or without evidence

quality_signature_cohesion_scored.instructions: Are all 11 signature/cohesion items (S1-S7, H1-H4) scored 0/50/100 with one-line justification each?

labels.no: Some items missing scores or justifications

quality_section_ledger_complete.instructions: Is the Section Ledger complete? Every major section has a verdict (CLEAN/SUSPICIOUS/INFLATED/CRITICAL) with tell count and action?

quality_signature_gate_applied.instructions: Is the Signature gate applied correctly? If Axis 7 < 40, overall must be capped at 59.

labels.yes: Signature gate correctly applied (or not triggered)
labels.no: Signature gate should apply but wasn't

quality_absolute_gate_applied.instructions: Is the Absolute-rule gate applied correctly? If any critical tell exists, overall must be capped at 69.

labels.yes: Absolute-rule gate correctly applied (or not triggered)
labels.no: Absolute-rule gate should apply but wasn't

quality_compounding_cap_applied.instructions: Is the Compounding cap applied correctly? If ≥3 major layout tells, Axis 4 must be capped at 40.

labels.yes: Compounding cap correctly applied (or not triggered)
labels.no: Compounding cap should apply but wasn't

quality_math_from_script.instructions: Was all scoring done via score.py, never hand-computed?

quality_template_followed.instructions: Does the report structure match output-template.md exactly?

quality_fixes_ranked.instructions: Are fixes ranked by weighted impact? Signature issues (3x weight) typically outrank single tells.

quality_language_correct.instructions: Is the report in user's language with tell IDs kept in English for greppability?

quality_obvious_slop_flagged.instructions: Self-audit: 'What still looks like obvious slop that I didn't flag?' — if something visually screams slop but isn't in findings, either find the tell that covers it or note it as a catalog gap.

quality_over_correction_checked.instructions: Self-audit: 'Did I over-correct?' — a sparse report on clearly-slop design suggests missed tells. A bloated report on premium design suggests false positives.

labels.yes: Report density appropriate to design quality

quality_trust_test.instructions: Self-audit: 'Would I trust this report if someone else wrote it?' — read the report as if reviewing a colleague's work. Does every claim hold up?

labels.no: Report has claims that don't hold up

usage_notes.axes_1_6: Tell-counted axes (1-6) use score.py with tell counts by severity. Jev is NOT used for these — tells are factual (cite-or-cut), not subjective.
usage_notes.axes_7_8: Signature and Cohesion axes use Jev Score questions. Each element gets 0/50/100 with calibrated assessment.
usage_notes.quality_checklist: Noul questions for binary verification. All should be 'yes' before delivering the report.
usage_notes.integration: Jev supplements, does not replace, the existing scoring system. score.py handles tell arithmetic; Jev handles subjective rubric scoring.
